chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Dawud ibn Muhammad al-Nahdi, from some of our companions, who said: Ibn Abi Sa'id al-Makkar entered upon al-Rida (peace be upon him).

He said to him: 'Has Allah raised your rank to the point that you claim what your father claimed?' He said to him: 'What is wrong with you? May Allah extinguish your light and bring poverty into your home. Do you not know that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed to Imran (peace be upon him): "Indeed, I am gifting to you a male"? So He gifted him Maryam, and He gifted Maryam Isa. Thus, Isa is from Maryam, and Maryam is from Isa, and Maryam and Isa are one thing. Similarly, I am from my father, and my father is from me, and I and my father are one thing.'

He said to him: 'O Ibn Abi Sa'id, shall I ask you about a matter?' He said: 'I do not think you will accept from me, and you are not from my followers, but bring it.' He said: 'A man said at his death: "Every slave of mine who is old, he is free, for the sake of Allah."' He said: 'Yes, indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says in His Book: "until it returns like the old date stalk." Therefore, whoever of his slaves has been with him for six months is considered old and is free.'
Then the man went out and became poor until he died, and he did not have a place to sleep for even one night. May Allah curse him.

key_terms.ابن أبي سعيد المكاري: Ibn Abi Sa'id al-Makkar, a companion known for his literalist or sometimes tricky interpretations
key_terms.العرجون القديم: The old date stalk, a Quranic phrase used here to define the duration of 'oldness'
key_terms.عمران عليه السلام: Imran, the father of Maryam, to whom Allah revealed the gift of a son
key_terms.مبيت ليلة: A place to sleep for a night, indicating extreme poverty

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Rida define the term 'old' for emancipating slaves based on the Quranic verse 'like the old date stalk'?
ai.summary: This narrative from *Mani al-Akhbar* illustrates the dialectical method of Imam al-Rida (AS) by contrasting a literalist misunderstanding of divine unity with a precise legal application of Quranic terminology. While Ibn Abi Sa'id incorrectly equates the ontological relationship of Maryam and Isa to that of father and son, the Imam demonstrates that 'old' (*qadim*) in the context of emancipation refers to a specific temporal duration of six months, as derived from the metaphor in Surah Ya-Sin. The story serves as a critique of superficial scriptural interpretation, showing how rigid literalism can lead to financial ruin, a fate befalling the challenger who freed his slaves based on this narrow definition.
